title: UCL Grant Museum catalogue chronology and card-index provenance router
purpose: Route the unresolved Science Museum-to-UCL Blaschka transfer problem through the Grant Museum's successive documentation systems, preserving the 1890/1891 catalogue-date discrepancy and treating historical card indices as the highest-value bridge across the 1925-1927 transfer window.
relationship_to_auction_layer: This is provenance infrastructure only. Institutional transfers recovered through UCL documentation remain outside the canonical auction count.

date_labels.current_ucl_blaschka_highlight: 1890 printed museum catalogue compiled by E. Ray Lankester
date_labels.ucl_2013_documentation_history: first catalogue published by E. Ray Lankester in 1891

documentation_chronology.document_character: UCL's documentation-history blog describes it as part catalogue, part wishlist; another UCL collections-history discussion likewise warns that some listed objects may never have entered the collection.
documentation_chronology.research_use: Recover the twenty Blaschka appearances and compare their historical names/model numbers against current accessions, but require corroboration before treating a catalogue appearance as physical acquisition.

documentation_chronology.description: UCL's 2013 documentation-history account states that the second cataloguing attempt was a card-index series begun in the early 1900s and continued until the 1970s.
documentation_chronology.provenance_value: This documentation layer spans the Science Museum 1925-1927 Blaschka transfer window and therefore has a higher probability than the 1890/1891 catalogue of recording later acquisitions, source institutions, renumbering or labels for transfer-derived models.

documentation_chronology.description: UCL identifies Museum Documentation Association cards as the third major cataloguing attempt. A 2013 project processed about 1,500 handwritten MDA cards and cross-referenced them with the current catalogue.
documentation_chronology.data_quality_note: UCL states that some specimens have multiple cards with different or conflicting information.
documentation_chronology.provenance_value: MDA cards may preserve acquisition/source data inherited from earlier card systems or object labels even when those fields are absent from the public Axiell record.

documentation_chronology.description: Electronic systems followed the card-index layers. Current Collections Online is explicitly an ongoing catalogue and UCL does not present it as complete.
documentation_chronology.provenance_value: Useful public access point but not an exhaustion test for old provenance or transferred-object identifiers.

historical_information_loss_problem.ucl_statement: UCL staff describe collection information as distributed across archives, paper notes, object surfaces, labels, inventories, photographs, article reprints and successive catalogue systems that do not perfectly overlap.
historical_information_loss_problem.methodological_effect: A missing field in Collections Online is not evidence that the museum never recorded it. Provenance work must query multiple documentation generations.

target_material: object files/labels for eight named accessions
research_request_packet.specific_question: Which current Blaschka accessions entered from the Science Museum in 1925-1927, and what old Science Museum or South Kensington numbers survive in the documentation?
research_request_packet.contact_route: UCL Museums and Collections / Grant Museum research enquiry; current UCL collections pages direct researchers to museum staff when online catalogue information is insufficient.
